emergent_bug.violated_requirement: ρ = atomic([read(total_elements)]) from thread_a (the lockless poll read must not be interleaved with a conflicting write)
emergent_bug.missing_guarantee: thread_b holds pool->lock during the write, but thread_a reads total_elements with NO lock; a one-sided lock does not serialize against an unlocked reader, so no g establishes atomic(read) on the poll side
emergent_bug.category_rationale: ρ is atomic over a single access (an unsynchronized read concurrent with a conflicting write) → data race

fix_maps_to: guard(spinlock_irq)(&pool->lock) added inside snd_seq_pool_poll_wait() (and the lockless caller-side check dropped) → adds serialize(pool->lock, poll read) to the reader → establishes atomic(read) by making both sides hold the same lock
recall_risk_notes: Structurally a clean unprotected-read-vs-locked-write race that our atomic(single access) default captures. Risk: the maintainer notes the race is HARMLESS (poll of volatile state); an LLM may judge the unprotected read benign and decline to assert atomic(read), which would suppress the report. Object/threads are static-friendly (same poll/ioctl fops, surface pre-fills total_elements + pool->lock candidate).
